name: The freight shed on the south bank below the Dearborn draw

documented_range.note: NO SOURCE RECORD IN THIS REPOSITORY DATES THIS BUILDING, BECAUSE NO SOURCE RECORD NAMES IT. The range is the reconstruction's own bracket and it is graded as one. It is the SAME bracket the four north-bank sheds of T-0133 carry, deliberately: it opens on 1834-08-01, the date `dearborn_street_drawbridge` opens on, because the reason to stand a freight shed on this reach is that the crossing brought the town's traffic to it, and it closes at the end of 1835 because nothing follows the building and a range that ran on would be claiming survival nobody attested. What IS held is the treatment, not the date: image 3 of the owner's brief of 2026-08-18 (data/sources/assets/owner_brief_2026_08_18/README.md) is an engraving of this reach from farther out, and it draws low warehouses on BOTH banks below the bridge. A tier-5 retrospective plate can attest that the banks below the draw carried working sheds; it cannot date one.

position.symbolic_location: On the south bank of the main stem below the Dearborn Street drawbridge, on the last town ground east of South Water Street's platted corridor and west of State Street's, standing back from the riverside plank walk on the terrace behind it, with its wagon door to the landward side and the walk and the river behind it.
position.note:
INVENTED, AND PLACED BY A RULE RATHER THAN BY A PLATE. The plate that puts sheds on this bank is image 3 of the owner's brief of 2026-08-18 (data/sources/assets/owner_brief_2026_08_18/README.md): masts crowd the reach below the bridge, a light structure near the mouth, LOW WAREHOUSES ON THE BANKS. It is a TIER-5 PICTORIAL source — retrospective, drawn decades after 1835 — and this project's standing rule for one is that it may drive massing, form, materials and setting and may NEVER drive a coordinate. So the plate decides that a shed stands on this bank and nothing else about where.

RE-SEATED AND RE-SQUARED 2026-09-27 (T-1643), AND THE REASON IS WORSE THAN THE ONE THAT WAS FILED. The seating this record carried until today was read off the fort road — 1.25 m of setback from the north edge of its travelled way, squared to the road's bearing here, the wagon door to the road — and T-1637 moved that road off this reach hours after the seating was written. This record said so at the time, and said correctly that re-seating was a change of geometry and its own question rather than something to smuggle into the run that moved the road. THIS IS THE ANSWER TO THAT QUESTION, and it is not the tidy-up it was filed as: the position the road had chosen stood ACROSS THE TOWN'S OWN RIVERSIDE PLANK WALK. The walk's east end — river_plank_walk_crossing_footway in data/frontage/river_walk_frontage.json — runs from local E 803.6 to E 815.0 at N 14.2 and is 1.83 m wide, so its boards occupy N 13.285 to N 15.115; the footprint seated by T-1636 spanned N 8.164 to N 18.455 and took the whole width of them. NO DATASET GATE COULD SEE IT, and that is the second half of the finding: a walk is boards laid on ground this project has already built and a building is a mesh seated on the same ground, and nothing compared the two. What found it was the published walker: standing on the walk at E 809.4, N 14.2 and walking west, a visitor was pushed out of the shed's collision footprint east to E 811.5 instead of reaching E 802, and that check had been red on dev from the moment the shed was seated. tools/measure_south_bank_ground.py now masks the committed frontage walks as well as the unplatted travelled ways, and refuses outright any committed building on this reach that stands on a walk, so the reading that admitted this station cannot admit it again. NOTHING ABOUT THE EVIDENCE CHANGES HERE: the plate, the grade, the bracket, the size and the total working uncertainty are what they were. What changes is the three numbers that were read off a line that has gone — the northing, the bearing and the door's side — and they are now read off a line that is here.

WHY THIS BANK CARRIES A SHED AT ALL, AND IT IS A MEASUREMENT AND NOT A CHANGE OF MIND. T-0134 measured the whole reach — dearborn_street_drawbridge (local E 699.2) east to the Reservation's west line (E 842.0) — and found NOT ONE position, at any bearing, where the smallest footprint family F1 allows would stand on dry ground outside a platted corridor with less than 0.35 m of relief. The south bank was refused on that reading and the refusal is recorded in data/exclusions.json as `south_bank_warehouses_dearborn_reach`. T-1629 then re-traced the town slough's mouth to Wright's own re-entrant east of State Street and FILLED the mouth this project had cut west of it, and the ground that had been the old channel and its approach cuts came up about a metre above the water and dead flat. T-1636 re-read the reach on that ground: 91 positions appeared at 0.30 m of relief where there had been none. tools/measure_south_bank_ground.py is the reading and tools/south_bank_ground_baseline.json is what it is held to. THE READING STILL ADMITS THIS GROUND, and it is asked again with the walk masked: at the nearest station on the reading's own one-metre lattice, E 806.0 / N 2.0 at bearing 0, the same rectangle stands free at 0.30 m of relief and clear of every board. This record's own seat is the rule below's answer, half a metre west of that station and 0.47 m south of it.

WHERE IS DERIVED, from three committed things and one stated setback. (1) THE EASTING IS UNCHANGED IN RULE, and it is the one number T-1637 left checkable: the westernmost station on the reading's own half-metre lattice, between South Water Street's platted corridor and State Street's, at which the whole rectangle stands on free ground. Squared to the walk that station puts the west wall at local E 805.5. Half a metre west of it the rectangle's west side is inside South Water's corridor; where it stands the tightest point of the building is 0.30 m clear of that corridor, at the north-west corner, and 3.81 m clear of State Street's on the other side. It is not chosen for the view: it is the first ground east of the platted town. (2) THE NORTHING AND THE BEARING COME OFF THE RIVERSIDE PLANK WALK, which is the committed line that is still on this reach and the one line this building has to be clear of. The walk's boards end at N 13.285; the north wall stands 2.00 m back from that edge at N 11.285, which is 2.915 m from the walk's centreline; and the walls are squared to the walk's own bearing at this station, which is due east, so rotation_deg is 180.000 and the long axis runs back from the bank. (3) THE COMMITTED HEIGHTFIELD, data/terrain/epochs/e1834_harbor_cut: sampled on the same half-metre lattice the reading uses, 252 points, the ground under this footprint stands between 1.189 m and 1.286 m above the water surface — 0.097 m of relief across the whole rectangle, well inside the 0.30 m `generate_block_infill.MAX_RELIEF_M` allows — so the walls share one walker surface without a cut or a fill.

THE SETBACK IS NO LONGER A CONCESSION, AND THAT IS WORTH SAYING BECAUSE THE OLD SEAT MADE ONE. Set back from the fort road this building could not keep the 2.00 m the four north-bank sheds keep from North Water Street's travelled edge: at 2.00 m its back wall fell half a metre further down the bank and the rectangle's relief reached 0.353 m, past the clause, so the setback came in to 1.25 m and both figures were stated so the trade stayed visible. On the terrace south of the walk the trade does not arise. This building now keeps the north bank's own 2.00 m, at 0.097 m of relief against the 0.273 m the old seat carried, so the reach's two shed rows are set back by the same figure for the first time.

WHAT IT STANDS INSIDE, SAID PLAINLY: nothing. The fort road's reconstructed 12 m corridor left this reach with the road (T-1637) and fort_road's committed path now begins at E 826.8, twenty-one metres east of this building's east wall. tools/measure_corridor_intrusion.py reads the footprint clear of all 33 platted corridors. It stands on no committed walk, and tools/measure_south_bank_ground.py --gate is what says so on every commit.

HOW A CART REACHES IT, because the old note answered that with a road that has gone. South Water Street's platted corridor ends 0.30 m west of this building's west wall, and that street is the only made approach to this ground: a cart comes east out of its end onto the flat terrace the filled channel left, and stands on the landward side of the shed, which is the side the wagon door is on. The door faces due south, AWAY FROM THE BOARDS: the walk is a 1.83 m footway and it is the one thing a visitor does on this bank, so loading across it is the mistake this re-seating is undoing and not one to re-make at a smaller scale. It is the same arrangement the four north-bank sheds keep, whose doors face their street and whose backs are to the water.

WORKING UNCERTAINTY: total. Nothing states that a building stood at this station on 1835-07-01. What would replace this placement is a lot record on the river side of South Water Street, a forwarding merchant's advertisement giving an address on this reach, or a contemporary view of the south bank. docs/LIBERTIES.md owns the invention.

derivation.reason: The two machine-checkable methods this project has are a platted corner and a traced waterline, and this placement is neither: it is a setback from the committed centreline of the riverside plank walk plus a relief test against the committed heightfield, at the westernmost easting the two platted corridors either side of it leave free. All three inputs are committed and the rule is stated in full in position.note, so it is reproducible by hand — which is what T-1637 took away when it moved the line the northing and bearing used to be read off, and what T-1643 gave back by reading them off a line that is still here. No derivation method in the schema can recompute it, and declaring one that could not would be worse than declaring none.

footprint.note: INVENTED AT THE SMALLEST SIZE THE PROGRAMME'S BAND FOR THE FAMILY ALLOWS, because it is the only size this ground takes. 5.4864 x 9.7536 m is 18 x 32 ft, the floor of family F1 (freight or storage shed) in data/reconstruction/1835_building_inventory.json, whose band runs to 28 x 50 ft. It is also the exact rectangle `tools/measure_south_bank_ground.py` sweeps the reach with, so the building and the reading that admitted it are the same size and the placement can be checked against the reading that found it. The frontage is the short side and the depth runs back from the door, which is the crosswalk's own description of F1 — a long building with wide doors — and what the plate's low sheds read as. The long axis cannot run along the bank instead: 9.7536 m of frontage does not fit between South Water Street's platted corridor and State Street's, which are 9.5 m apart on this bank, and re-seated square to the riverside walk (T-1643) the building's 5.4864 m of frontage uses 5.49 m of that 9.5 m window with 0.30 m clear of one corridor and 3.81 m of the other. No source gives this building a dimension because no source gives this building.

construction.note: The crosswalk's F1 entry gives 'vertical-board frame' for a freight shed, which is the archetype's `plank`: sawn boards nailed up vertically with the gaps showing. The same treatment the four north-bank sheds of T-0133 carry, because the plate draws the two banks' buildings alike. Invented either way — nothing states how any building on this bank was built.

wall_height_m.note: The crosswalk's F1 eave band is 10-13 ft (3.05-3.96 m) and this is 11.2 ft, inside it and a little lower than the north bank's 3.6 m. A cart and a stacked load set the floor; the plate's word for these buildings is LOW and that sets the ceiling, and the smallest footprint in the family carries the lowest eave in it rather than the same one a building half again its size carries. Invented.

roof_type.note: F1's roof line in the crosswalk is 'gable or shed'. Gable, which is the near-universal roof of a frame building of this type and date, and the roof the north-bank row carries. Invented.

roof_pitch_deg.note: F1's pitch band is 5:12 to 9:12, which is 22.6 to 36.9 degrees; this is 30.0 degrees, inside it and the same as the north bank's. No source gives a pitch for anything on this bank. Invented.

door.note: A freight shed is a building goods go into and out of by cart, so the opening is the archetype's `wagon` door rather than a man door — which is also what the crosswalk's F1 entry means by 'wide doors; low openings'. Until T-1643 this note said the only way a cart reaches this ground is the fort road; that road left the reach with T-1637, and the only made approach now is South Water Street's own east end, which stops 0.30 m west of this building's west wall. The door is on the landward side, facing the flat terrace a cart comes out onto, and not on the riverside walk's 1.83 m of boards. Invented, like the building.

door_side.note: The door faces the landward side — the side a cart can come from, out of South Water Street's east end onto the terrace — and not the river side, where the town's riverside plank walk runs 2.00 m off the back wall and loading would block it. Re-read by T-1643: until then this said the door faced the fort road, which T-1637 moved off the reach, and the seating that answer produced stood across the walk itself. The two platted corridors are at either end of the building, so those two sides were never candidates. The archetype's front faces north at rotation 0 and this record is rotated 180 degrees, square to the walk, so `front` here is the south wall and the back wall is the one the walk and the river are behind. Invented.

paint.note: Unpainted boards, which is the archetype's own default and the treatment image 3 and image 11 both show on working river buildings. Paint on a freight shed would be the larger claim. Invented.

phases.change_note: One phase. This building is a reconstruction of a TYPE the plate puts on this bank, not a record of a building anybody named, so it has no history to divide into phases and inventing one would be inventing twice.

function.note: The use comes from the plate and from the place. Image 3 of the owner's brief of 2026-08-18 draws low warehouses on the banks of the reach below the drawbridge, and this reach is where the river traffic, the town's only crossing of the main stem and the road to the fort all met in July 1835. The specific goods, the trade and the operator are not inferred and are not recorded: an occupant would be a person, and this record claims a building.

research_note: A RECONSTRUCTED BUILDING, AND THE SECOND HALF OF T-0134 — the half that finding said it could not take. T-0133 built the four north-bank sheds image 3 of the owner's brief draws and left this bank empty, with one sentence in all four of their records: the platted South Water Street corridor reaches to within about 1.7 m of the traced 1834 waterline at the Dearborn reach, so there is no ground there for a building that is not standing in the platted street. T-0134 turned that spot reading into a command over the whole reach and the refusal held, harder: not one position at any bearing, at 0.30 m of relief or at 0.35 m. THAT SENTENCE IS STILL TRUE OF THE FRONTAGE THE PLATE DRAWS, and this building does not stand on it. Beside the platted street — west of South Water's own east end at local E 805.0 — the reading is still zero at every relief clause it is reported at, and one clause HARDER than when the refusal was written: the three positions that used to stand there at a metre of relief are gone. What changed is east of the street's end. T-1629 re-traced the town slough to Wright's own re-entrant east of State Street and filled the mouth this project had cut west of it; the old channel and its approach cuts came up flat and dry, and T-1636 re-read the reach. Ten positions clear of the fort road's travelled way, at 0.30 m of relief, on ground that had been a channel of this project's own making. This is the westernmost of them. WHAT IS HELD: image 3 of the brief (data/sources/assets/owner_brief_2026_08_18/README.md), an engraving of the reach below the Dearborn drawbridge showing low warehouses on BOTH banks; and image 11, the retrospective painting of South Water Street in 1834, which shows what a working river frontage in this town looked like. Both are tier-5 pictorial and neither is yet held as a source record — T-0075 owns that — so this record cites committed paths rather than a source_id, and no source is claimed. WHAT IS CONJECTURAL: the building, its station, its size, its construction, its roof, its opening and its date. All of it, as on the north bank. WHAT WOULD UPGRADE IT: a lot record on the river side of South Water Street, a forwarding merchant's advertisement giving an address on this reach, or a contemporary view of the south bank. Built under the owner's standing ruling of 2026-08-18 — 'you are totally fine to be liberal with adding reconstructed items when i ask for things, you can just label and mark them as such'. RE-SEATED 2026-09-27 BY T-1643, AND THE REASON IS A DEFECT AND NOT A REFINEMENT: the station T-1636 chose stood across the full 1.83 m width of the town's riverside plank walk, so a visitor walking the bank was pushed out of the building instead of past it. The northing and the bearing are now read off the walk's own committed centreline instead of off the fort road T-1637 moved away, and the building stands 2.00 m back from the boards on the terrace behind them. Nothing about the evidence moved: the plate, the grade, the bracket and the size are what they were, and the working uncertainty is still total.
